sources.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: ensure
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Selected result/condition sense; Word Origin. The current verb concerns making an outcome or condition definite. Its French history is reported as connected to earlier assure forms. That historical relationship alone does not decide a current teaching split. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: en- prefix
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Verb-forming prefix, causative sense 2. The modern prefix has a causative reading used before an adjective base. Its location/condition sense is separately described. This is the prefix entry, not the -en suffix entry. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: sure adjective
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Result-certainty uses and make sure sense 1. The base expresses certainty, including outcomes certain to occur. The make-sure entry distinguishes bringing about a result from checking a fact; the candidate selects the result reading. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Collins dictionaries: ensure
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Selected outcome sense and American English word history. The whole-word result meaning aligns with the accepted candidate. Word history explicitly links en- with a French predecessor of sure. This corroborates the base boundary while remaining historical evidence. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Collins dictionaries: en- prefix
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: British English en- 1 causative sense; American English prefix. Causative use on adjective/noun bases is current. The entry describes productive English formation modeled on French loans and separately distinguishes the Greek in/within prefix and -en suffix. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: inform
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Recipient-information sense, verb forms and Word Origin. Current giving-information and influence meanings are separate. The forms include informed and informing. Historical development concerns shaping or forming the mind, through an into-prefix and form/shape base; it is not negative in- or a document-form meaning. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: informed adjective
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Knowledgeable person/state and decision based on understanding. The adjective includes having knowledge and a decision grounded in understanding. This supports a plausible family relation to inform while showing why having been told something alone does not settle an informed decision or clinical consent. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: collect verb
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Bring-together sense, distinct take-away sense, verb forms and Word Origin. The selected sense brings items together from several sources; pickup is separate. Forms retain collect before inflections. The historical chain passes through Latin collect- and colligere, with together and gather/choose elements. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.

sources.title: Collins dictionaries: collect
sources.scope: Fresh author consultation: Selected gathering sense, verb forms and verb word history. Gathering from several people/places is distinct from pickup and payment meanings. Historical analysis describes Latin col-/com-, legere and participial development. The prayer noun and unrelated senses are excluded from the proposal. Morphology and canonical-family decisions require independent review; no lexical, clinical, media or release approval is granted.
